*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: .weekday_analysis.py
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+con = duckdb.connect()
+source = str(ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet")
+
+data = con.execute(
+    """
+    WITH weekday_counts AS (
+        SELECT
+            dayofweek(crash_date) AS dow,
+            count(*) AS crashes
+        FROM read_parquet(?)
+        WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+          AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+        GROUP BY dow
+    ), weekday_dates AS (
+        SELECT dayofweek(d) AS dow, count(*) AS dates
+        FROM generate_series(DATE '2013-01-01', DATE '2025-12-31', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS t(d)
+        GROUP BY dow
+    )
+    SELECT
+        c.dow,
+        CASE c.dow
+            WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday'
+            WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday'
+            WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday'
+        END AS weekday,
+        c.crashes,
+        d.dates AS weekday_dates,
+        c.crashes::DOUBLE / d.dates AS crashes_per_date
+    FROM weekday_counts c
+    JOIN weekday_dates d USING (dow)
+    ORDER BY CASE c.dow WHEN 1 THEN 1 WHEN 2 THEN 2 WHEN 3 THEN 3
+             WHEN 4 THEN 4 WHEN 5 THEN 5 WHEN 6 THEN 6 WHEN 0 THEN 7 END
+    """,
+    [source],
+).df()
+
+total = int(data["crashes"].sum())
+data["share_percent"] = data["crashes"] / total * 100
+data[["weekday", "crashes", "share_percent"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+data[["weekday", "crashes", "weekday_dates", "crashes_per_date"]].to_csv(
+    OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f"
+)
+
+plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid")
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.8))
+bars = ax.bar(data["weekday"], data["crashes"], color="#2676a5")
+ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[f"{v:,.0f}" for v in data["crashes"]], padding=3, fontsize=9)
+ax.set_title("NYC police-reported crashes by day of week\n2013–2025", fontsize=15, pad=14)
+ax.set_ylabel("Crashes")
+ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+ax.set_ylim(0, data["crashes"].max() * 1.12)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=15)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.8))
+bars = ax.bar(data["weekday"], data["crashes_per_date"], color="#d17a22")
+ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[f"{v:,.1f}" for v in data["crashes_per_date"]], padding=3, fontsize=9)
+ax.set_title("Average NYC crashes per calendar date, by weekday\n2013–2025", fontsize=15, pad=14)
+ax.set_ylabel("Average crashes per occurrence of weekday")
+ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+ax.set_ylim(0, data["crashes_per_date"].max() * 1.12)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=15)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+print(data.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Total crashes: {total}")
+print(f"Date range: {con.execute('SELECT min(crash_date), max(crash_date) FROM read_parquet(?) WHERE crash_date >= DATE \'2013-01-01\' AND crash_date < DATE \'2026-01-01\'', [source]).fetchone()}")
*** End Patch

+      "probability": 0.65,
+      "answer": "Friday had the most police-reported crashes (338,800; 15.9% of the total) and Sunday the fewest (257,544; 12.1%).",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how the total number of recorded crashes is distributed across weekdays, with Fridays highest and Sundays lowest. Pooled counts directly represent the observed crash records across the full requested period. It does not adjust for the number of calendar dates of each weekday or show how the pattern changed by year."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "metric": "Average police-reported crashes per calendar date",
+      "denominator": "Calendar-date occurrences of each weekday in 2013–2025 (678 or 679 dates, depending on weekday)",
+      "grouping": "Day of week, pooled across 2013–2025",
+      "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+      "reason": "Dividing by the number of dates of each weekday makes the weekday comparison account for their slightly different calendar-day exposure.",
+      "probability": 0.35,
+      "answer": "Friday averaged 499.7 crashes per date, the highest weekday average, while Sunday averaged 379.9, the lowest.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how the average number of crash records on a date differs by weekday, accounting for 678 or 679 occurrences of each weekday in the period. The per-date average still peaks Friday and reaches its low Sunday, so the count pattern is not explained by a weekday having more dates. It does not measure traffic volume or crash risk per trip, and it does not show year-to-year changes."
+    }
+  ]
+}
